title: Madama Butterfly
facts: Madama Butterfly premiered at La Scala on 17 February 1904 in a two-act version, and was withdrawn after a disastrous first night.
At the 1904 premiere, audience plants were given nightingale whistles for the sunrise. The audience took it as a cue to make animal noises of their own.
The premiere was called “one of the most terrible flops in the history of Italian opera”. One problem: no intermission in the very long second act.
Puccini’s sister Ramelde wrote that night: “The second act I didn’t hear at all, and before the opera was over, we ran out of the theater.”
Ramelde Puccini, letter to her husband, 1904 (via Wikipedia)
Puccini rewrote it, splitting the long second act in two. The new version was a great success in Brescia on 28 May 1904.
The Humming Chorus became the bridge between Puccini’s new Acts II and III.
There are five versions of Butterfly. Puccini’s final 1907 revision, the “Standard Version”, is the one usually performed.
Butterfly reached the Metropolitan Opera on 11 February 1907, in Puccini’s third version.
The first US performances, in 1906, were in English, by Henry Savage’s touring company.
From the long love duet that closes Act I: “Bimba dagli occhi pieni di malia”, “Sweetheart, with eyes full of enchantment”.
Sharpless brings a letter from Pinkerton asking him to break the news that he isn’t coming back to Japan.
“Il cannone del porto!”, the cannon at the harbor, leads into the famous Flower Duet.
The musical Miss Saigon (1989) was inspired by Madama Butterfly.
